defaultValue.value:
{
  "$comment": [
    "THE single source of truth for game rules. Loaded verbatim by the Unity",
    "client AND the .NET server; the server hashes it and stamps configHash on",
    "every run so a client on a stale config is rejected rather than silently",
    "scored against different rules.",
    "",
    "Requirement #16 of the brief is 'change the lane count from 4 to 5 live'.",
    "Nothing below hardcodes 4. Lane count is len(lanes); the road generator,",
    "the hitbox model, the input clamp and the UI all derive from this array."
  ],

  "configVersion": 1,

  "lanes": [
    { "index": 0, "multiplier": 5, "role": "scoring", "hazardWeight": 1.00 },
    { "index": 1, "multiplier": 2, "role": "scoring", "hazardWeight": 0.55 },
    { "index": 2, "multiplier": 1, "role": "scoring", "hazardWeight": 0.30 },
    { "index": 3, "multiplier": 0, "role": "cashout", "hazardWeight": 0.00 }
  ],
  "startLane": 2,

  "time": {
    "ticksPerSecond": 60,
    "$comment": "Fixed timestep. Render framerate must not affect the score.",
    "maxRunTicks": 10800,
    "$maxRunTicks": "How long a run may last before it ends as ABANDONED, and the hard ceiling on the server's replay of a submitted one. Shared and hashed because it decides an OUTCOME: it lived in the server-only economy file until the client shipped its own copy of the number, and the two disagreed - the client called a run ABANDONED at 1800 while the server replayed the same swipes to 10800 and recorded CRASHED. Both scored zero so no money moved, but the player was told one thing and the record said another. 10800 = 180s at 60Hz, matching money.noSubmission.windowSeconds: a run longer than the window it must be submitted within cannot settle anyway."
  },

  "speed": {
    "$comment": "Speed is a pure function of tick count. Fixed-point, units are milli-units/sec to keep the score accumulator integral.",
    "startMilliUnitsPerSec": 20000,
    "rampMilliUnitsPerSec": 500,
    "rampIntervalTicks": 30,
    "maxMilliUnitsPerSec": 55000
  },

  "laneChange": {
    "durationTicks": 12,
    "maxQueuedInputs": 1,
    "$multiplierRule": "During transit the effective multiplier is min(origin, destination). Closes the boundary-parking exploit.",
    "$hitboxRule": "During transit the hitbox occupies BOTH lanes.",
    "$reversalRule": "Reversal is always legal and takes effect on the tick it is received, never queued behind the in-flight move."
  },

  "player": {
    "carLengthUnits": 4,
    "$comment": "Hitbox length along the road. Collision is an integer interval overlap; during a lane change the car occupies this interval in BOTH lanes."
  },

  "hazards": {
    "trafficSpeedFactorMin": 0.45,
    "trafficSpeedFactorMax": 0.80,
    "spawnLeadUnits": 90,
    "$spawnLead": "Road distance AHEAD of the player at which a hazard appears. A hazard placed at the player's own position materialises on top of them with no warning, which is unavoidable-by-construction and reads as a bug. 90 units is roughly 1.6s of warning at the starting speed and about 4s of closing time on slower traffic.",
    "encounterIntervalTicks": 45,
    "maxEncounterWindowTicks": 600,
    "$encounter": "Hazards are placed on a tick cadence, not a distance cadence, because collision is evaluated per tick and moving traffic drifts across any distance-based bucket. maxEncounterWindowTicks bounds how long a single hazard can block its lane while being overtaken.",
    "minLongitudinalGapUnits": 12,
    "startRunwayUnits": 60,
    "$startRunway": "Road distance at the start of every run that carries no hazards. Without it the generator can place a hazard at position 0, killing the player on tick 0 before they have touched the screen - exactly the 'killed through no fault of their own' case the brief calls a refund request. 60 units is about 3 seconds at the starting speed: long enough to read the road, short enough not to be boring.",
    "obstacleLengthUnits": 3,
    "trafficLengthUnits": 5,
    "spawnChancePerSlice": 0.80,
    "trafficShare": 0.55,
    "$spawnChance": "Base probability that a lane receives a hazard in a given road slice, before being scaled by that lane's hazardWeight. Lane 0 at weight 1.00 therefore sees 0.80; the cashout lane at weight 0.00 never receives one - arriving there ends the run, so a hazard on it can only zero a player at the moment they go to bank, which reads as the game cheating.",
    "$trafficShare": "Of hazards spawned, the fraction that are moving traffic rather than static obstacles.",
    "$solvability": "The generator must never emit a longitudinal slice where no legal lane-change sequence survives. Tools/Solvability proves this over N seeds."
  },

  "scoring": {
    "$comment": "score += distanceTicks * multiplier, in fixed-point milli-units, floored to a whole number only for display. Never float.",
    "accumulator": "int64-milliunits"
  }
}

redline_game.description: Game rules. Byte-identical to Backend/config/redline.game.json; hashed and stamped on every match.

defaultValue.value:
{
  "$comment": "Server-authoritative money + rating + matchmaking config. Never shipped to the client except as a payout preview.",

  "money": {
    "currency": "USD",
    "$type": "All server-side money is INTEGER CENTS, authored as integers here and parsed as integers. No float, no decimal type, no rounding mode: every amount is a whole number of cents, exact up to 2^53, and every operation on it is integer arithmetic. parseEconomyConfig rejects a non-integer value naming the key.",
    "stakeCents": [50, 100, 200, 500, 1000],
    "rakeBasisPoints": 1000,
    "$rake": "1000 bp = 10%. potCents = stakeCents*2; rakeCents = divRoundHalfEven(potCents * bp, 10000) in integer arithmetic; payoutCents = potCents - rakeCents. Half-to-even, because away-from-zero would bias the half-cent toward the house on every match.",
    "tie": {
      "policy": "split-after-rake",
      "$applies": "Both players banked an identical score, OR both crashed (both scored 0). Both are ties; there is one rule, applied identically.",
      "$money": "rakeCents = divRoundHalfEven(potCents * rakeBp, 10000); remainder = potCents - rakeCents; each side receives floor(remainder / 2) cents.",
      "oddCentGoesTo": "poster",
      "$oddCent": "If remainder is an odd number of cents the extra cent goes to the POSTER, who set their number blind while the challenger knew the target. With the current stake ladder this never triggers (all splits are exact) but the rule is defined so the ledger can never fail to balance if stakes change.",
      "$rating": "Elo draw, S = 0.5 for both sides. Zero-sum, so ties cannot inflate or deflate the rating economy.",
      "$note": "Chosen over voiding the match so the house earns on every settled match. Known cost: both players finish slightly down on a match neither lost. Tie frequency is reported by Tools/Simulate; if double-crashes are common this rule should be revisited."
    },
    "noSubmission": {
    "policy": "forfeit-as-zero",
    "windowSeconds": 180,
    "$applies": "A player who staked and received a seed but produced no valid submission before the window closes.",
    "$money": "Settles as an ordinary loss. Stake is already debited; the opponent takes the pot less rake. No special money path.",
    "$rating": "Ordinary loss, S = 0.",
    "$outcome": "ABANDONED(0). The score of record is 0 — identical to crashing into a hazard.",
    "$why": "Intent is never inferred. A real phone crash and a deliberate force-quit are indistinguishable in principle, so the rule is built so that not submitting can never beat submitting: any completed run scores >= 0, so quitting is weakly dominated. This satisfies the brief's 'disconnect is not a strategy' without a detector that could be wrong.",
    "$bothSides": "If BOTH players fail to submit, both score 0, which is a tie and settles under money.tie.",
    "$knownGap": "A player on a genuinely broken device loses their stake. Accepted: the alternative (refund on non-submission) hands every losing player a free undo. Documented in the architecture doc under what we knowingly do not handle."
  },
  "challengeTtlSeconds": 900,
    "$expiry": "Full refund to poster, once. No rating movement for either side."
  },

  "roleAsymmetry": {
    "$comment": "The poster sets their number blind; the challenger would otherwise know it and bank one point above it. See DevDocs/decisions/0009-role-asymmetry.md for the arithmetic and the pre-registered prediction.",
    "hideTargetFromChallenger": true,
    "$hideTarget": "The server never sends a poster's banked score to a challenger whose run is unfinished. Enforced by omission, not by client-side hiding: a patched client shows whatever it is sent. Set false to reproduce the unmitigated behaviour for the control run in report section 6.",
    "$why": "With the target visible the poster's win rate is capped at 25% however well they play, because they can only choose their survival probability S and win with probability S*(1-S). That maximum is independent of the hazard shape. Hiding it makes both seats face the same blind decision.",
    "$alsoConsidered": "Alternating roles, weighting the Elo update by role, and a poster rake discount. All rejected in the ADR; only hiding the target actually equalises win rates at equal rating, which is the test the brief sets."
  },

  "rating": {
    "system": "elo",
    "initial": 1200,
    "floor": 100,
    "ceiling": null,
    "$ceiling": "No hard ceiling; justified in DevDocs/decisions. Elo is self-limiting because expectation saturates.",
    "provisionalMatches": 10,
    "kFactors": [
      { "maxMatches": 10, "k": 40, "$label": "provisional" },
      { "maxRating": 2100, "k": 24 },
      { "k": 16 }
    ],
    "leagues": { "count": 10, "boundaries": [800, 1000, 1150, 1250, 1350, 1450, 1600, 1800, 2100] },
    "seasonReset": { "mode": "soft", "keepWeight": 0.6, "anchor": 1200, "anchorWeight": 0.4 },
    "inactivity": { "mode": "none", "$comment": "Nothing happens to an idle rating, deliberately. 'freeze' was the wrong word: freeze is a real mechanism (lock the rating, or widen an uncertainty term) and we implement none of it. See DevDocs/decisions/0012-inactivity.md. Parsed by nothing — declarative only." }
  },

  "matchmaking": {
    "$comment": "Selection-and-ranking over a live inventory of posted challenges, NOT queue pairing.",
    "stakeMatch": "exact",
    "band": { "initial": 100, "widenPer10s": 25, "cap": 600 },
    "recentOpponent": { "maxMatches": 2, "windowHours": 24 },
    "newPlayerProtection": { "matches": 5, "excludeTopDecile": true },
    "collusion": {
      "sameAccount": "block",
      "sameDeviceFingerprint": "block",
      "samePaymentInstrument": "block",
      "sharedIpWindowMinutes": 60
    },
    "starvation": { "policy": "post-own-challenge", "$comment": "Never invent a bot opponent. Every opponent is a real account." }
  }
}
